To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the WAIS-III/WMS-III and WAIS-IV and the WMS-IV were designed to be used individually as well as in combination, that the factor structures for each instrument are known, and that the factor structure for the combined battery is not yet known.
the WAIS-4 and WMS-4 were co-normed and can be used as a combined battery.
two measurement models fit the data well: one model is a seven factor model without a hierarchical general factor and the second model is a 5-factor model with a hierarchical general factor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the factor structure of WAIS-IV and WMS-IV.
the identification of the factor structure of the WAIS/WMS co-norming battery.
the identification of a factor structure for the combined WAIS-IV and WMS-IV battery.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the WAIS- IV/WMS-IV is a reliable and valid measure of cognitive functioning and that the WAIS–IV/WMS- IV can be used to identify specific cognitive strengths and weaknesses.
the factor structure of the WAIS/WMS battery is a five-factor solution with a hierarchical general factor.
the WAIS- IV and the WMS-IV are two separate tests that can be used individually or in combination.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the WAIS-III/WMS-III and WAIS-IV/ WMS-IV are similar in that both batteries are comprised of seven independent factors.
both models are acceptable, but that the seven-factor model without a hierarchical general factor is preferable to the five-factor model with a hierarchical general factor.
the WAIS-III/WMS-III factor structure is maintained in the WAIS- IV/WMS-IV battery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the WAIS- IV/WMS-IV is not a single test but a battery of tests.
the WAIS- IV/WMS-IV is a complex battery of tests with many factors.
there is no one right way to interpret WAIS-IV and WMS-IV scores.
